analysis:
SanDisk fell 21.7%, 17.2 points more than the market's 4.4% decline, amid a broad AI and technology selloff. The stock moved roughly in line with its memory and storage peers, which saw a median decline of 17.0%, though SanDisk's drop was 4.7 points steeper. Headlines reference an "AI selloff" continuing despite SanDisk's strong earnings, a broader Nasdaq correction driven by data center anxiety, and sector-wide issues including memory-chip shortages at Micron causing ripple effects across the industry.

The company reported earnings one week ago on October 29, beating estimates by 6.7% but falling 13.5% the next session, with a 6.0-point abnormal move beyond what the market explained. This continues a pattern: across six recent reports with market data, SanDisk beat estimates every time yet posted a negative abnormal move in three cases, with a median abnormal reaction of 6.7 percentage points. The typical post-earnings move has been 6.8%, suggesting volatility around these events, though whether beats help has been inconsistent.
